lines.text: I. Brief History of the Laguna College
Don Zacarias Sahagun and Don Melecio Fule founded
the Laguna Academy in 1923 to provide secondary schooling to
the people of San Pablo City and its neighboring towns.
Starting with just sixteen students, the school soon grew and
expanded under the competent leadership of its succeeding
administrators: Dr. Nicasio Sahagun, Mrs. Gertrudis S.
Evangelista, Mr. Alfredo Y. Evangelista and Miss Natividad S.
Evangelista. Today, it offers kindergarten, elementary, science
high school: special science and K-12 curriculum, college, short-
term courses, and graduate school courses which, together,
make up a student population of several thousands. Its new
name -- Laguna College -- is a household word today. In 1996, it
was granted Accreditation Status (Level II) for its courses in
Liberal Arts, Education and Commerce by the PACUCOA
(Philippine Association of Colleges and Universities-Commission
on Accreditation). It was re-accredited for the fourth time for Level
II in 2019.
II. The Mission of the Laguna College
Laguna College does its best to impart and promote
knowledge of the arts and sciences, to instill love of country and
to protect the people's liberty.
It spares no effort in cultivating the many good Filipino values
of charity, justice, truth, honesty, decency and compassion.
It goes to great lengths to hire the best teachers available
and to provide the best facilities and equipment its resources can
afford, in order to produce graduates who are honest, decent and
responsible citizens, fully dedicated to the creation of a just,
humane and caring society that fears God, protects the
environment and serves the cause of the country and the world.
III. The Vision of the Laguna College
The Laguna College will be the best school to provide
education that is comparative locally, nationally and globally.

A. Admission Policies
The Laguna College is open to students with satisfactory academic
work and valid entrance credentials. The applicants should pass the
entrance examination given by the guidance office for the level he/she is
applying for, subject to the availability of accommodation and facilities of
the school. Kindergarten and grade one pupils must meet the DepEd age
requirements.
The students, having been admitted to the Laguna College and
having completed his/her enrollment, agree to abide by the rules and
regulations set by the College. The basis of the admission policies set by
the College is the belief that only those students whose qualifications
indicate a strong likelihood of success and who can measure up to its
academic standards in the course they are enrolled, should be accepted.
As a general rule, therefore, the Laguna College admits only those
enrollees who possess good moral character, personal integrity, and
maturity of purpose and behavior befitting a student.
The school reserves the right to refuse enrollment or re-enrollment to
the following:
1. Pupils/Students who have physical or mental illness, contagious
disease or other sickness as certified by the school physician which
may be aggravated by the burden of academic studies.
2. Students with disciplinary cases considered grave by the
committee on discipline
2.1. Students who have participated in, incited, caused, or led acts of
violence, vandalism, and other forms of utter disregard for law
and order.
2.2. Students known to be or to have been associated with
elements, groups, or movements that tend to subvert the
country's democratic institutions.

lines.text: C. Registration Procedures
1. Students are advised to read the enrollment procedures. These
procedures must be strictly followed to insure facility in enrollment and
the proper filing of their enrollment forms.
2. Students must enroll on the days designated for their academic years
to facilitate enrolment. Enrollment schedules may vary from semester to
semester. Students are asked to consult the bulletin board before the
start of each term.
3. The Laguna College does not guarantee the availability of particular
subject(s) or sections thereof. Students are enrolled in classes until the
allowable maximum number of students has been reached.
4. The college reserves the right to cancel sections already programmed
due to insufficient number of students or other necessitating
circumstances. No charge is imposed for changing subjects in such a
case.
5. When a pupil/student fails to pay debts, the college may withhold re-
enrollment and other services, such as grades, certification, and
transcript of records of F-138 and F-137 until the debts are paid.
6. The college reserves the right to determine whether a credential
submitted will be accepted as official. Credentials submitted become
part of the student's permanent record and cannot be withdrawn after
registration has been completed.
7. Students are not allowed to enroll in advanced subjects before
they have completed the corresponding pre-requisite subjects of the
preceding year or semester.
8. No credits will be given to subjects not validly enrolled or
registered, subjects taken without the corresponding pre-requisite
subject and subjects or units in excess of the regular load not authorized
as per CHED regulations.
9. Students are allowed to attend only the classes in which
they are enrolled or registered.
10. Cross-registrations outside the college by students in their last semester
may be permitted with the prior written approval of the Dean concerned
and the Registrar. No credit shall be given for any work done if the
permit has not been secured.

D. Probationary Status of Transferees
All transferees shall be under probationary status once
admitted as students in the institution. They shall be placed under
this status for one (1) full academic year. During this period,
transferees who obtained failing grades in most of their subjects
and who have violated school rules and regulation shall no longer be
admitted in the succeeding semester.
E. Fees
1. Tuition fees and other charges are prescribed by the College
with the approval of the Department of Education or the
Commission on Higher Education. Notice of increase in fees is
published in advance.
2. Tuition fees in the Elementary and Junior High School are paid
in six (6) installments, while those in Senior High School and
Collegiate courses are paid in five (5) installments per
semester, with the first installment in all levels and courses paid
upon enrollment.
3. Tuition fees during summer classes are paid in full.
4. Tuition fees for Masteral students are paid in four (4) installments
per semester.

as far as refunds and grades are concerned, is the date the dropping
form is filed in the Registrar's office.

VII. Class Attendance
1. A student who has incurred absences of more than 20% of the
required total number of class and laboratory periods in a given
term or semester shall be dropped from the course or subject.
2. No student who has been absent from classes for three (3)
consecutive days shall be admitted without presenting to the
instructor concerned an excuse slip duly signed by his/her parent or
guardian. The excuse slip must be countersigned by his/her
principal, dean or Guidance Counselor. In case of absence due to
sickness for 3 days or more, the student should present a medical
certificate countersigned by the school physician.
3. A student is required to be punctual and regular in his class
attendance. He/She must be in the classroom on time. Tardiness of
more than 10 minutes without justifiable reason shall be considered
an absence.

final examination, submitting term paper, project, etc.

1. The required completion fee has to be paid to the Cashier's Office.
The Official Receipt serves as permit for the completion of an
incomplete grade and should be presented to the instructor
together with the completion form.

signed by the subject instructor, the Dean and the Registrar. A
completion grade is valid if the completion form is validated by
the Accounting Section and is submitted to the Registrar's Office in
due time. A grade of INCOMPLETE not completed within one year
is automatically given a rating of 70%. The basis of the period of
completion is the end of the semester when the student obtained
an INC mark.

completion form within one year to the Registrar's Office or

fees in full. Policies on Part IV, Section E of this Hand book shall

A. College
Rules on Scholarships
Both grades and financial standing of the students are used as
considerations for granting scholarship. These rules apply for
Academic Scholarship granted by this institution:
Grades
1. A student who has a weighted average of 95% and above is
entitled to Full Scholarship, 100% discount from tuition fees,
provided he/she has no grade lower than 88% in all subjects
taken.
2. A student with a weighted average of 92% to 94% is entitled to
Half Scholarship, 50% discount from tuition fees, provided
he/she has no grade lower than 85% in all subjects taken.
3. A student with a weighted average of 90% to 91% is entitled to
Partial Scholarship, 25% discount from tuition fees, provided
he/she has no grade lower than 80% in all subjects taken.
Units Load Requirements
A student to qualify for scholarship should have earned not less
than 18 units except when the required units for the particular semester
is less than 18, as certified by the College Registrar.
Special Provisions
1. Grades will be computed up to the second decimal place.
2. No student who has been punished for any act whether major,
serious or less serious offense in the school rules and regulations
on discipline shall qualify for scholarship.
B. Elementary and Junior High School
When a student ranks first in his/her batch in the previous school
year at Laguna College, the student receives 100% discount on tuition
fees. A student who ranks second in the batch shall receive 50%
discount on tuition fee.

lines.text: Article III - Behavior in Libraries
Rules and regulations governing the use of the library shall be
followed. The following rules and regulations govern the use of the
College library:
1. Silence must be observed at all times.
2. The main library is an "open stack" library. Thus, the
students may gain access to the library books anytime and
properly return them to the shelves or the circulation desk.
Avoid hiding books so that others may also gain access.
3. Readers must show their ID card at the desk and library
cards upon borrowing and at the request of the librarian.
Visiting researchers should have identification papers and
must register with the office of the Chief Librarian.
4. For those with circulation privileges, a book is allowed out
for one week. Renewal may be granted if the book is not in
demand.
5. Reserve books, Open Reserves - Books used as
accompanying reading for course work have unlimited use
in the reading room. This collection is located in open
shelves in the Reserved Section and may be there without
being signed out.
Close-Reserves - Books in demand prescribed for
courses are charged out at the loan desk and limited from
one to two hours and overnight use. Books borrowed
overnight may be checked out at 6:00 P.M. and should be
returned at 9:00 the following morning.
Article IV Behavior in Corridors
Section 1. Students shall not loiter or make any disturbance in
the corridors during class hours.
Section 2. Students shall keep to the right when walking in the
corridors and stairways.

lines.text: C. Campus Organizations
The formation of educational, cultural and scientific
organizations among students is encouraged.
To achieve official status, an organization must be approved
and recognized by the Administration. Official recognition may be
given after a process which includes:
1. Submission of written application (with the organization's
name and objectives, constitution and by laws, a list of all
the members, names of advisers who must be full-time
instructors, and affiliation) to the Campus Organizations
Screening Board.
2. Recommendation by the Campus Organizations
Screening Board to be submitted to the School
Administration.
3. Final approval by the School Administration.
Recognition granted to an organization may be cancelled by
the Administration if the organization in question has been found
guilty of violating regulations of the school and/or not fulfilling its
avowed aim or aims. Recognition is for one-year period, renewable
at the start of another school year if the organization has been found
satisfactorily complying with the rules and regulations of the school.
A list of members and their advisers, old and new alike, must be
submitted to the Administration upon application of renewal.
Student leaders are responsible, and are subject to
corresponding punishment under the principle of command
responsibility, for any violation of the rules and regulations
committed, with or without their consent or knowledge, by their
organization or members thereof.
The failure of any recognized student organization to comply
with prescribed requirements shall be sufficient cause for the
School Administration to take appropriate disciplinary action
against the student officers concerned or to withdraw or cancel the
recognition granted to such student organization.
